item.title: Re: Data not redacted? (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

See…my core concern here is that there's not really a sense of consequences/stakes here: like, it's fine to have the ethics committee be secretly be behind this but there's not really a like…clear feeling of there being a motivation for it, and it doesn't really feel like it leads them to achieve anything or to the reader's understanding of this being significantly changed.

Like, it being a power play to allow the EC to gain an upper hand over the O5 council is fine but there's not really a clear idea of:

  1. why the EC wants to do this
  2. whether the EC are actually successful
  3. what the EC are going to do if it is successful

My feelings are that if this is to work, you'll likely want to actually make the EC/O5 interplay part of the text because it's the interesting part of this but it's also the part which actually feels like it has stakes; and in turn, you'll need to really consider what the framing is that allows you to do this: it's very possible to have the reader be canonically on one or the other as they read this; and in turn, to have partial information about what the other wants.

I don't think the current framing works because it relies too much on the mystery of this being interesting inherently without you doing anything to show why the mystery matters. This said: it's very possible that this is just my opinion and other reviewers will disagree.

item.title: Re: Data not redacted? (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
This feels very reminiscent of stuff like SCP-5242 or Allison Eckhart and I'm sure there's something that plays with the core a lot more closely than either of those; and so I'm left feeling very much like this needs to do a touch more with the idea.

The angle of this being like, the Ethics Committee trying to get the upper hand over the O5's is a pretty good angle and I think it could really help this work but I don't really have a feel for how this article is going to convey that: it's kinda thrown in as a possibility in the hook section; but like, are you going to be somewhat explicit about this? Are you just going to hint towards it? Is it just a possible hypothesis you think a reader might come up with?

I guess at the end of the day, my core question is really: so what are you doing with this? There's like a lot of like, vague hypothesises mentioned in this and they all sound vaguely interesting but I don't really have an idea of how this is all going to come together to form a cohesive article that actually like, tells a story, y'know?

item.title: Re: Data not redacted?
item.content:encoded:
The narrative is shown primarily through the discovery log, and towards the end it is only implied that it isn't just a GoI but the Ethics Committee. Is this a correct summary?

More crit below!
Oh no!

The narrative of the discovery laid out in the forum is; a junior researcher discovers the anomaly, and brings it to the attention of the senior researcher.

Other than this, there is no other narrative described.

I once was given the crit; "[…]if you don't reveal the story you want to tell, we won't know how to help you!"

I realise that you wish to keep parts of it vague for the readers sake, but at the moment this is an idea concept thread, and its totally ok to reveal these "spoilers"!

My advice is to not worry about spoilers, and reveals, until you have a second or third draft.

We can agree to disagree! Just wanted you to know a little more of my thoughts. I hope this helps!

item.title: Re: Data not redacted?
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for sharing this in IRC!

Crit below!
Geronimo!

The concept reads as familiar. I believe there is an SCP article similar to this concept (my apologies for not remembering the specifics. I believe it was localised to censoring itself though). You can refer to it as a phenomena or object, as an entity it would still be a phenomena.

Part of the hook should be in the central narrative (Ethics Committee essentially black mailing/sabotaging the O5 command).

Your hook is the censorship and corruption itself. In the central narrative, what is the narrative with the GoI and the junior researcher (what I'm asking is not both of them together, but each instance on its own)?

The elevator pitch is a bit long, and as a reader, it’s a giant block of text that I don’t want to engage with. The elevator pitch, in general, is a sales pitch. You; as a writer, are selling us; the readers, on reading the piece- and to engage with the post. Sell us; the readers, on the article. Show us why we should take the time to read it.

I like the hook and concept, but other than that this is lacking too much narrative for me to care as a reader to read the article if it were on the mainlist.

item.title: Data not redacted?
item.content:encoded:
Something or someone is censoring information on foundation database and it is spreading to all known copies including pyhsical ones.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Classic article

Elevator Pitch: Idea is that something is "corrupting" Foundation database with random censors like ████ or [DATA REDACTED] while the censored information was known before and cant be find anywhere including any physical copies of it. This phenomenon is somehow spreading to other articles.

At first look it may look like a error or maybe GoI spies, but with some logical explanations and different theories threat is something different.

Central Narrative: It gives several theories and hypothesis about whats the reason or whats the behind it after the discovery. Discovery of it starts by junior researcher that leads to researcher collague to the site director after they agree its not a simple error and at the final to the one of the O5's. With that investigations start with help of web crawlers.

In short central narrative will be about its discovery and leads to its current state (with some dialogues), while foundation giving several theories about what or how this is happening and why.(With table wizard)

example: Solution is [DATA REDACTED] (It has been censored due to being possible cognitohazard.)

In article it says this censor effects everyone except Ethics Comittee. (Including O-5's) There are 2 different reasons for it. 1st one is; we know that ethics comittee can read all type of censor hence it doesnt affect them somehow.

2nd reason is much more radical, and this scp is nothing but Ethics Comittee doing. Why would they do that you may think? Reason is they want to gain upper-hand againsts O-5's on power shift between them. They know that they are on constant power war. They know that they can censor everything they want and no one would question them.
